title: The Byrock Story
description: A premium, achievement-led account of Byrock Technologies, the evolution of its laminitis platform, and the development path behind PTP-102.

nodes.title: Byrock Technologies
nodes.summary: Byrock Technologies is a founder-led biotechnology company built around a long scientific arc: enzyme inhibition, antibody science, laminitis biology, and the translation of that insight into practical veterinary development. Its lead public program, PTP-102, brings this history into a defined equine laminitis focus, combining a serious unmet clinical need with a modern therapeutic-development mindset. The Byrock story is one of persistence, scientific refinement, and the movement from early platform thinking toward a more focused, evidence-led program for horses at risk of one of the most challenging conditions in equine medicine.

media.alt: Dark premium biotech cover visual with the Byrock Technologies identity, subtle cyan linework, and a connection between equine health and therapeutic science.

nodes.title: The Unmet Need in Laminitis
nodes.summary: Laminitis is one of the most serious challenges in equine health. It affects the hoof-supporting lamellar tissues and can rapidly progress from pain and lameness to structural failure, prolonged recovery, major welfare concerns, and loss of athletic or breeding value. That clinical burden is exactly why Byrock has focused here. The opportunity is meaningful: improve the way the disease is approached, support earlier and more targeted intervention, and help build a stronger evidence base for a condition where veterinarians, owners, trainers, and breeders still need better options.

media.alt: Illustrated horse profile with the hoof region highlighted in a restrained clinical infographic style.

nodes.title: The Scientific Rationale
nodes.summary: The scientific foundation behind PTP-102 is the laminitis cascade itself: inflammatory activation, metalloprotease activity, oxidative stress, lipid peroxidation, and disruption of the lamellar architecture that supports the hoof. PTP-102 is built around methylated tirilazad, a 21-aminosteroid lazaroid class compound associated with antioxidant and membrane-stabilizing activity. Byrock’s central insight is that protecting lamellar tissue may require targeting the destructive biology early, rather than simply managing pain after damage has progressed. That mechanism-led approach gives the program its scientific coherence and its development focus.

media.alt: Simplified mechanism diagram showing inflammatory and tissue-damaging pathways involved in laminitis with an investigational intervention point.

nodes.title: From PTP-100 to PTP-102
nodes.summary: The PTP platform shows a clear progression of scientific refinement. PTP-100 began with camelid antibody and plasma-derived thinking, focused on the inflammatory and proteolytic drivers implicated in laminitis. PTP-101 moved the concept toward a more defined synthetic peptide approach aimed at metalloprotease inhibition. PTP-102 then advanced the platform again, centering the program on methylated tirilazad and a synthetic 21-aminosteroid strategy. The result is a strong development narrative: Byrock has moved from broad biologic insight to a more focused, practical, and chemically defined therapeutic candidate.

media.alt: Three-step timeline showing the evolution of the Byrock laminitis platform from PTP-100 through PTP-101 to PTP-102.

nodes.title: Research Evidence to Date
nodes.summary: Byrock’s evidence package has developed across multiple layers: earlier controlled ETCR work around PTP-100, lamellar explant and in-vitro investigations, internal study summaries, formulation work, and a 2024 peer-reviewed publication describing methylated tirilazad / PTP-102 in an oligofructose-induced laminitis model. The achievement is not just a single result; it is the assembly of a coherent scientific dossier. Together, these materials support a serious development case, connect the biology to observable laminitis outcomes, and give Byrock a foundation for more disciplined clinical and regulatory progression.

nodes.title: Regulatory Pathway
nodes.summary: Byrock has moved the PTP-102 program beyond concept work and into structured development planning. The regulatory story includes product-development thinking, formulation and manufacturing considerations, investigational-supply logistics, patent positioning, and veterinary regulatory engagement. This is where the company’s work becomes more than science: it becomes a product pathway. The priority now is to keep strengthening the package with clean study data, site discipline, adverse-event capture, stability information, and documentation that supports the next stage of professional review and partner engagement.

nodes.title: How the Program Is Being Studied
nodes.summary: The study strategy is designed around practical veterinary evidence: appropriate case selection, treatment timing, Obel lameness scoring, hoof-related observations, clinical follow-up, safety monitoring, and supporting tissue or biomarker analysis where available. Byrock’s strongest next step is disciplined execution: every treated case should produce usable clinical documentation, not just anecdote. That means time-stamped observations, clear baseline status, defined treatment windows, adverse-event tracking, and structured follow-up. This approach turns promising science into credible, partner-ready evidence.

nodes.title: The Team Behind Byrock
nodes.summary: Byrock is built around founder-led invention supported by clinical, veterinary, operational, legal, and corporate experience. Patrick T. Prendergast, PhD, anchors the company as Founder and Inventor, bringing decades of scientific and biotechnology experience to the laminitis platform. Dr. Daniel Shanahan-Prendergast, MD, supports the medical and clinical-development narrative. Cormac Jones coordinates project development and external engagement. Dr. Julio Cesar Prado, DVM, contributes veterinary clinical-trials perspective, while Anthony Joyce supports legal and corporate matters. The team connects invention, clinical translation, operational follow-through, and strategic execution.

media.alt: Portrait-led team spread with a featured founder card and supporting leadership cards using consistent cyan and red rim lighting.

nodes.title: Patrick T. Prendergast, PhD
nodes.summary: Patrick T. Prendergast, PhD, is the scientific origin point of the Byrock story. His background spans microbiology, genetics, virology, antiviral development, antibody science, enzyme inhibition, and biotechnology venture creation. Across multiple decades, his work has repeatedly returned to the same core idea: identify damaging biological pathways, find ways to inhibit or modify them, and translate that insight into therapeutic programs. The evolution from PTP-100 through PTP-102 reflects that pattern clearly, carrying Patrick’s long-running focus on enzyme-targeting science into a concentrated equine laminitis program.

media.alt: Founder spotlight featuring Patrick T. Prendergast, PhD, with a short scientific career summary and a path from invention to platform evolution.

nodes.title: Pipeline and What Comes Next
nodes.summary: PTP-102 is Byrock’s lead public program and the clearest expression of the company’s current direction. The path ahead is focused and valuable: deepen the evidence package, tighten clinical documentation, strengthen manufacturing and formulation data, progress regulatory planning, and engage the right veterinary, commercial, and strategic partners. The broader platform story remains important, but the public message should stay sharp: Byrock has taken years of scientific development and concentrated it into a lead equine laminitis program with a credible scientific rationale and a clear next-stage development agenda.
